content: 1. It is essential to provide the patient with information about available services and ensure she can access them independently. 2. In role play 1, focus on listening attentively to the patient’s relative to fully understand her concerns. Consider the best ways to connect her with appropriate services and support systems. 3. During discussions with bereaved families, remember they are grieving. Allow them the space to express their emotions and talk about their loved one. 4. Inform the family about the high risk of infection for anyone who comes into contact with the deceased person’s body. 5. Gently explore whether anyone in the household may have been exposed to Ebola while caring for the deceased during their illness or through contact with their body or belongings. 6. Stress the importance of going to the hospital to determine their health status and prevent further spread of infection. Highlight that early detection and supportive treatments significantly improve survival rates. 7. Provide accurate information about safe burial practices and dispel any rumors. 8. Discuss alternative burial rituals and safe ways to mourn and honor their loved one. 9. In role play 2, emphasize the dual need to support the family emotionally while also preventing the spread of infection. 10. Take safety precautions when approaching the family, such as avoiding entering their home. 11. Help the family understand the importance of household members being tested for Ebola to prevent further transmission. 12. Offer to connect them with services and support systems. 13. When caring for children, remain calm, speak softly, and be kind. Introduce yourself by name, reassure them that you are healthy, and explain that you are there to help. 14. Ask the child’s name, age, where they are from, and gather information about their family or caregivers. 15. Communicate with the child at their eye level and use language and explanations they can understand based on their age and developmental stage. 16. If the child is unaccompanied, stay with them while arranging for appropriate caregivers or child protection services. 17. Spend time listening, talking, and playing with children, ensuring activities are age-appropriate and adhere to Ebola safety precautions. 18. If speaking with a child who has Ebola, explain that while you cannot touch them, you are there to listen and care about their feelings. 19. In role play 3, emphasize the importance of approaching children kindly and using age-appropriate language. Do not leave the child alone until they are reunited with family or linked to a trusted child protection agency. 20. Highlight the special needs of children during an Ebola outbreak, including their vulnerability due to disrupted routines, loss of family, stigma, and discrimination. 21. Explain that children cope better when they have a stable, calm adult around them. 22. Children with suspected Ebola should always be accompanied to a hospital, health post, or designated care center. 23. If a parent requires medical attention, ensure that their children are cared for and not left to fend for themselves. 24. Encourage participants to work with trusted child protection agencies to reunite children with families or caregivers. 25. Do not attempt to handle child protection issues alone, as mistakes can worsen the child’s situation. 26. Provide handouts with information on how children of different ages respond to crises and how caregivers can support them. 27. Explain that people with health conditions or disabilities may face worsened conditions during an Ebola outbreak due to overloaded health systems and reduced access to care. 28. Assist individuals with health conditions or disabilities in finding a safe place, meeting basic needs, accessing medications or treatments, and connecting with protection and care agencies. 29. Avoid physical contact with individuals showing Ebola symptoms and refer them for immediate medical care. 30. Discuss the risks of discrimination and violence during an Ebola outbreak, particularly for women, certain ethnic or religious groups, and people with disabilities. 31. Explain that health workers, surveillance teams, burial teams, and relatives of Ebola victims may also face stigma and violence. 32. Help at-risk individuals find safe places, connect with loved ones or trusted people, access information and services, and receive immediate medical attention if needed. 33. Emphasize the importance of not worsening stigma or discrimination while helping others. 34. Highlight the need for self-care and team care for helpers during an Ebola outbreak to ensure they can assist others effectively. 35. Encourage helpers to manage stress by maintaining healthy work and life habits, taking breaks, and seeking support from colleagues and loved ones. 36. Remind helpers that they are not responsible for solving all problems but are there to help people help themselves. 37. Stress the importance of preparing to help by learning about Ebola, understanding safety measures, and considering personal health and stressors. 38. Encourage helpers to make honest decisions about their readiness to assist in specific situations. 39. During the outbreak, helpers should manage stress by eating, resting, and relaxing, keeping reasonable working hours, and minimizing alcohol, caffeine, or nicotine use. 40. After helping, take time to rest, recover, and reflect. 41. Encourage small group discussions among participants to share strategies for self-care and team care before, during, and after helping in an Ebola outbreak. 42. Recap the importance of self-care and team care, emphasizing that helpers must prioritize their physical and emotional well-being to assist others effectively.
